Whatever one thinks of cloning and its potentially scary sci-fi connotations, one cannot diminish the ingenuity and sheer bloody tenacity of embryologist Sir Ian Wilmut and his Roslin colleagues. To produce Dolly, the team transferred 277 cell nuclei into the eggs of Scottish blackface sheep—from these only one live lamb was born. Mammalian cloning was not the stuff of tech-bro efficiency.

Twenty years ago, Steve Irwin was pierced through the chest by a short-tail stingray while filming a snorkeling dive at Batt Reef near Queensland, Australia, causing him to go into cardiac arrest.
